questions.question: What is Three-Phase Commit (3PC)?

options.text: An extension of 2PC that adds a pre-commit phase to reduce blocking

questions.explanation: 3PC: adds 'pre-commit' phase between prepare and commit. Reduces blocking: participants can make progress even if coordinator fails. Phases: CanCommit → PreCommit → DoCommit.

questions.question: What problem does 3PC solve that 2PC doesn't?

options.text: The blocking problem—participants can timeout and make progress if coordinator fails

questions.explanation: 2PC blocking: if coordinator fails after prepare, participants stuck. 3PC: pre-commit phase ensures all participants know the decision before commit. On timeout, participants can safely abort or commit.

questions.question: What are the three phases in 3PC?

options.text: CanCommit (voting), PreCommit (prepare to commit), DoCommit (actual commit)

questions.explanation: 3PC phases: 1) CanCommit: coordinator asks if participants can commit. 2) PreCommit: if all yes, prepare to commit. 3) DoCommit: actually commit. Pre-commit ensures everyone knows decision before committing.

questions.question: Why is 3PC rarely used in practice?

options.text: Higher latency (3 round trips), doesn't handle network partitions well, complexity

questions.explanation: 3PC drawbacks: 3 round trips (vs 2 for 2PC), still fails under network partitions (split-brain possible), added complexity. In practice, other solutions (Paxos, Raft, Saga) preferred.

questions.question: How does the pre-commit phase help with blocking?

options.text: All participants know the decision before commit, so they can safely proceed on coordinator failure

questions.explanation: Pre-commit key insight: if participant received pre-commit, it knows coordinator decided to commit. On timeout, can safely commit. If no pre-commit received, can safely abort. Eliminates uncertainty.

questions.question: What happens in 3PC if a participant times out during pre-commit?

options.text: Participant can abort—if it didn't receive pre-commit, coordinator must have decided to abort

questions.explanation: Timeout during pre-commit: participant hasn't received pre-commit, so coordinator either failed or decided to abort. Safe to abort. This is the non-blocking property 3PC provides.

questions.question: Can 3PC handle network partitions?

options.text: No—network partitions can still cause inconsistency (split-brain)

questions.explanation: 3PC partition problem: one partition might commit (received pre-commit), another might abort (timed out). Split-brain. 3PC assumes fail-stop (crash), not network partitions. Real networks have partitions.

questions.question: What is the latency overhead of 3PC compared to 2PC?

options.text: One additional round trip (3 phases vs 2 phases)

questions.explanation: 3PC latency: 3 round trips minimum (CanCommit, PreCommit, DoCommit) vs 2PC's 2 round trips. 50% more latency. In distributed systems where latency matters, this is significant.

questions.question: What is the relationship between 3PC and consensus algorithms like Paxos?

options.text: Paxos handles partitions correctly; 3PC doesn't—Paxos is preferred for real systems

questions.explanation: Paxos/Raft: handle network partitions correctly, provide consensus. 3PC: non-blocking but fails under partitions. Modern systems use Paxos/Raft for coordination, not 3PC. 3PC is mostly academic.

questions.question: In what scenario would 3PC work correctly?

options.text: Fail-stop model—nodes crash but network is reliable (no partitions)

questions.explanation: 3PC assumes fail-stop: nodes either work or crash completely, network delivers messages. In this model, 3PC is non-blocking. Real networks have partitions, message loss—3PC assumptions don't hold.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of 3PC over 2PC?

options.text: Non-blocking—participants can make progress without coordinator in fail-stop model

questions.explanation: 3PC advantage: non-blocking in fail-stop model. Participants can timeout and decide (abort or commit) without waiting for coordinator forever. 2PC can block indefinitely on coordinator failure.

questions.question: Why do modern distributed databases not use 3PC?

options.text: Network partitions are common; 3PC doesn't handle them; Paxos/Raft are better

questions.explanation: Modern systems face network partitions. 3PC fails under partitions (split-brain). Paxos/Raft: proven correct under partitions, widely implemented. Spanner uses Paxos, CockroachDB uses Raft. 3PC is historical.
